headline: The pairformer trunk is not a 13.0x wall and never was a 46.67x product defect. Both of its tracks are reachable today -- the pair track as shipped, the single track under a flag that is already landed and deliberately held -- and what is actually left is one measurement nobody has taken: its gradient against a 0.4.3 reference.

revision.rigour: 2 of 2 release trees built and run in full, 2736 of 2736 tensors loaded into each with 0 missing and 0 unexpected, whole-tree digests pinned before loading (0.4.3 1b27f575, 0.5.0 092fb575 byte-identical to the sdist), and the digest routine given a break control first -- pointed at the parent directory it now fails loudly, where its first version reported ABSENT for the six files that decide the function and returned a correct-looking whole-tree digest anyway.

orientation.finding: tt-bio ships the RIGHT bias orientation for this checkpoint. 0.4.3's `TriangleAttention.forward` takes no `transpose_bias` argument at all and builds the bias from the already-transposed x; 0.5.0 adds the argument and `PairBlock.tri_att_end` passes True. Read from source BEFORE any fold ran, then measured: 0.4.3 == 0.5.0-with-the-flag-off at rel_l2 0.000000e+00, bit-exact.
orientation.the_trap_it_avoided: OpenFold zero-initialises `mha.linear_o`, so a freshly constructed layer emits an identically zero tensor and every rel_l2 reads 0/0 -- a comparison that cannot fail. Caught by drawing one weight set into both layers and asserting the output norms non-zero (2.018379 and 2.018795) before reading any ratio.
orientation.consequence: the arm labelled `fix` in perf/of3t_foldab/ is a MISNOMER -- it is 0.5.0's convention applied to a preview2 checkpoint. Its 0.435 A on 1UBQ and 1.332 A on a shallow-MSA 117 aa target measure what applying the WRONG release's convention costs, not damage the shipped path carries. OF3Trunk resolves `tri_att_end_bias_follows_pair = not is_openbind(state_dict)`, so preview2 gets 0.4.3's orientation and OpenBind gets 0.5.0's: each checkpoint gets its own release's convention and the wiring is right on both.

single_track.finding: the remaining single-track failure is NOT a precision loss. It is `scale_pair_bias=False` (D1). AttentionPairBias folds the pair bias inside its own score scale, (q.k^T + z) * d**-0.5, so a reference adding the bias UNSCALED needs it pre-baked by sqrt(head_dim); not pre-baking leaves the token pair bias at 1/sqrt(24) = 0.2041 of the reference value in all 48 blocks.
single_track.float64_identity: with the bias pre-scaled the single-track update reproduces upstream 0.4.3 at rel 7.882e-17 / 2.993e-16 / 4.204e-16 / 8.579e-16 at blocks 8 / 44 / 45 / 46 -- an identity, not a fit
single_track.why_it_looked_like_a_cliff: the single track's own growth collapses the logits. |q.k|max falls 13916.7 -> 6366.7 -> 975.1 -> 873.5 over blocks 8/44/45/46 while |bias|max only moves 53.88 -> 83.21 -> 29.44 -> 22.75, so bias/q.k goes 0.0039 -> 0.0131 -> 0.0302 -> 0.0260. A bias 4.899x too small is invisible at 0.4 % of the logits and dominant at 3 %, and the error tracks that ratio one for one.
single_track.on_device: scale_pair_bias=True alongside the existing tri_att_scale_pair_bias=False: single track 1.065338e-01 -> 1.655263e-02, inside both the 5.0e-02 bar and A26's 7.071068e-02; pair track BIT-IDENTICAL (z norm 1040888.017681702 in both arms), which is what a flag reaching one of the layer's two kernels must do
single_track.residual_after_the_flip: 1.655263e-02 is 2.48x upstream's own composed bf16 (6.681863e-03), above A26's reachable sqrt(2) -- genuine bf16 excess remains, 35x smaller than the convention was

the_product_question_this_leaves_and_it_: our port DELIBERATELY computes a different function from upstream at the trunk's token attention, because computing upstream's function serves 0.149 A worse at rank 0 -- and the reason it serves worse is D10, a separate defect in the confidence head's ranking. For inference that is a defensible trade and of3t-confhead made it on delivered structures. For a TRAINING-REPRODUCTION claim it is load-bearing in a way it is not for inference: you cannot reproduce a training step for a function you do not compute. That is why of3t-trunkg043 reads the FLIPPED arm as the scope's reading and reports the SHIPPED arm beside it, rather than either flipping a default or quietly scoring the arm we ship.
an_error_of_mine_caught_in_the_same_pass: my first draft of D114 filed the single-track deficit as UNFIXED and the campaign's sharpest remaining defect, proposed re-running `s_fp32_residual` (already refuted twice by of3t-rebase with the lever shown firing), and dispatched a row named `of3t-trunkcliff` to root-cause it -- a slug that already existed, concluded, having root-caused it. Caught by grepping concluded rows' VERDICTS for the slug before writing the brief. The name I invented independently was the name the row that already answered the question had been given, because it described the phenomenon.
